stem: A substrate settles and becomes noticeably denser during the crop cycle while the irrigation program remains unchanged. What root-zone effect should be evaluated?
choices: Evaluate changes in pore structure, drainage, aeration, and water retention because compaction can make the original irrigation assumptions less accurate
Evaluate the fertilizer label first because changes in media density mainly affect nutrient concentration rather than physical water behavior, then adjust the feed recipe before irrigation
Evaluate canopy color as the primary indicator because root-zone structure normally remains stable after the initial transplant period
Evaluate whether EC meters should be replaced because denser media can interfere with conductivity readings while leaving drainage unchanged
rationale: Settling and compaction can alter pore structure and therefore change drainage, aeration, and water retention. Irrigation assumptions should be rechecked when media physical behavior changes.
